Kernel `interval_make_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

**UNVERIFIED: no proof is checked.** The statement below is a target: Rocq has not checked a proof of it. No public operation calls it yet ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#proved-and-unverified)).

## What it computes

The interval of two values of `T`, or the whole line when a bound is a NaN, or the empty set when they describe none:

$$Z = [l_o, h_i].$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $l_o$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $h_i$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ is a canonical interval.
- If $l_o \le h_i$, $l_o < +\infty$ and $h_i > -\infty$: $Z$ is $[l_o, h_i]$, the same extended real numbers (a zero may change its sign).
- If a bound is a NaN, whatever the other: $Z$ is the whole line, $[-\infty, +\infty]$.
- Otherwise ($l_o > h_i$, $[+\infty, +\infty]$, $[-\infty, -\infty]$): $Z$ is the empty set, $(+\infty, -\infty)$.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**UNVERIFIED.** No proof of the statement is checked. The [Proofs](../proofs/index.md#what-is-proved-and-in-which-model) page says which statements of the IEEE model are proved against statements written by hand; this page gives the status that `gen/claims.json` gives.

## Source

**Algorithm:** constructor of an interval (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_make_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_make_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# An interval from two values of T supplied by the program, guarded (rule R3); milestone2.md,
# "Interval kernels", "Values of an interval": [lo, hi] when lo <= hi, lo < +inf and hi > -inf;
# the whole line when a bound is a NaN, whatever the other bound is (decided on 2026-11-20: a NaN
# says that something failed upstream, and the empty set must not come out of that); the empty set
# otherwise, that is for lo > hi, [+inf, +inf] and [-inf, -inf]. For every precision.

gl = guard(lo)
gu = guard(hi)
ok = le(gl, gu)
nl = lt(gl, const inf)
mi = neg(const inf)
nu = lt(mi, gu)
va = and(ok, nl)
v  = and(va, nu)
ql = eq(gl, gl)
qu = eq(gu, gu)
nn = and(ql, qu)
el = select(nn, const inf, mi)
eu = select(nn, mi, const inf)
zl = select(v, gl, el)
zu = select(v, gu, eu)
```
